title: Buying the Bones of a Fine Horse
text:
King Zhao of Yan came to the throne of a state that had just been ravaged by its neighbor Qi. He wanted to attract able men to help him rebuild and take revenge, and he asked the scholar Guo Wei how to do it. Guo Wei answered with a story.

A ruler of old offered a thousand pieces of gold for a horse that could run a thousand li in a day. Three years passed and no such horse was found. One of his attendants asked to try. Within three months he found one, but it had already died. He bought its head for five hundred pieces of gold and brought it back.

The ruler was furious at paying so much for a dead horse. The attendant explained that if the king would pay five hundred for a dead one, the world would conclude he would pay far more for a live one, and the horses would come. Within a year, three horses of a thousand li were brought to him.

"If Your Majesty truly wants to attract talent," Guo Wei said, "begin with me. If even I am honored, how much more will better men come." The king built a residence for Guo Wei and treated him as his teacher. Soon able men, among them the general Yue Yi, came to Yan from other states.
lesson: People decide whether to join you by watching how you treat those already with you. Visible respect for modest contributors is the best advertisement for attracting great ones.
people: Guo Wei, King Zhao of Yan, Yue Yi
source: Zhanguo Ce (Strategies of the Warring States), Yan
